rationale: Start with a broad, mid-temperature scouting gradient to maximize the chance that all 6 compounds elute within 42 min while revealing the full elution window and any critical adjacent pairs. All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only way to improve CRF is to reduce t_last. Halving tG while keeping the same wide window and temperature should pull the last peak earlier and test how much resolution margin we can trade for speed.

We already have the maximum CRF, so now the objective is to find the shortest method that still keeps every adjacent pair at R at least 1.5. Reducing tG one more step at the same window and temperature directly probes the speed limit while starting from ample resolution margin.

Resolution is still comfortably above threshold, so shorten the gradient again to see how far cycle time can be reduced before the first pair approaches R = 1.5. Keeping phi0, phi1, and T fixed isolates the effect of slope on the current worst pair.

The current worst pair still has substantial margin, so another 2-minute reduction in tG is the fastest way to locate the shortest acceptable method. This continues the controlled slope series and checks whether resolution remains above 1.5 under a very steep gradient.

At tG = 4 min the limiting pair is just above the 1.5 threshold, so testing the minimum allowed tG will show whether the absolute shortest gradient still preserves full-credit resolution. This is the cleanest next step because only slope changes and the current margin is small enough to expect an informative boundary test.

The boundary is now clear: tG = 4 min works and tG = 2 min is too steep because the first pair collapses. At tG = 4, trimming the high-end window slightly should keep all compounds eluting while making the effective gradient shallower and giving a little more margin on the critical early pair without sacrificing a still-short run.

The last peak still elutes well within the gradient window, so phi1 can likely be lowered further. Narrowing the window another step at tG = 4 should further shallow the gradient and may reveal the tightest efficient window that still keeps all 6 peaks out by the end of the gradient.

Lowering phi1 from 0.90 to 0.85 improved the critical pair while only slightly increasing t_last, so continue trimming the upper window. This should further shallow the gradient around the observed elution region and test whether we can gain more resolution margin with only a small time penalty.

The pattern remains favorable: each step down in phi1 increases the margin on the limiting first pair while t_last stays very short. Another reduction to phi1 = 0.75 should tell us how tightly we can bracket the actual elution window before the last compound begins to push too far into the hold.

The last peak is still eluting within the gradient and every reduction in phi1 has improved the worst-pair resolution, so the upper window can be tightened further. At phi1 = 0.70 the last peak is still comfortably within the gradient end, so one more step down in phi1 is worthwhile. This should further improve the limiting early-pair spacing while checking where the upper bound starts to slow the most retained compound disproportionately.

Now that the high-end window has been explored, probe whether the low-end can be raised to speed the earliest peaks without sacrificing full resolution. Moving phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 at the same short tG and broad phi1 should show whether the critical first pair is overly retained by the current low starting composition.

The earliest peaks are now very close to the dead-time region but still resolved above threshold, and raising phi0 has not hurt the overall pattern. At phi0 = 0.20 the first peak is nearing the unretained region, but the critical pair still has some margin and the run is slightly faster. One more step to phi0 = 0.25 tests the practical upper limit before early elution or pair compression becomes unacceptable.

The run is now very fast, but the first peak is approaching the near-unretained region and the limiting pair is close to threshold. A final step to phi0 = 0.30 will determine whether this is the highest starting strength still compatible with full-credit resolution.

The narrow-window trend at phi0 = 0.25 is improving the limiting pair with only a modest increase in t_last, so another step to phi1 = 0.80 is justified. This checks whether we can gain additional resolution robustness while still staying far below the 10-minute penalty limit.

The trend remains monotonic: lowering phi1 at phi0 = 0.25 steadily increases the worst-pair resolution while keeping the method very short. Testing phi1 = 0.75 will show whether this faster-starting window can also be tightened substantially at the high end without losing practicality.

This is the next logical extension of the successful phi1-trimming series at the fastest proven starting composition. It should indicate whether the high-end window can be narrowed to 0.70 while still keeping all compounds well within a short, fully resolved run.

The last peak is still well before 10 minutes and the limiting pair keeps improving as phi1 drops, so one more step to 0.65 is still low risk and informative. This explores the tightest high-end window likely to remain practical at the fastest successful phi0.
